newsitem.title: SPAIN: At least 21 killed in Spain train wreck.
newsitem.headline: At least 21 killed in Spain train wreck.

text.p: A crowded passenger train derailed in northern Spain on Monday night, killing at least 21 people, injuring 79 and trapping screaming passengers in the wreckage, officials said.

Authorities said the death toll could rise as rescue crews searched through the twisted metal in one of Spain's worst train accidents in recent decades. Eighteen of the injured were listed in serious condition.

The train, carrying 248 passengers, was travelling from Barcelona to Irun on Spain's border with France when three of its four carriages slid off the track and rolled over in the village of Huarte Araquil, about 32 km (19 miles) northwest of the city of Pamplona.
There were moments of stark terror in the overturned carriages as passengers, many returning from a long holiday weekend, struggled to crawl out from beneath piles of glass, baggage and broken seats.
"The people inside were screaming. It was horrifying," one woman passenger told reporters.
Dozens of ambulances rushed to the scene from nearby towns, and the survivors were eventually pulled free. But authorities feared more bodies might still be trapped inside.
There were so many wounded to attend to that emergency crews had to leave many of the bodies alongside the tracks wrapped in blankets. A makeshift morgue was set up in a nearby park.
"The number of people dead at this moment is 21," said a spokesman for the Spanish railway company RENFE.
State radio quoted Civil Guard officials as saying the accident was caused by "excessive speed."
RENFE officials said an investigation was under way but it was too early to determine the exact cause of the wreck.

The train, called the "Miguel de Unamuno", was changing tracks as it entered Huarte Araquil station and trying to speed in ahead of another train scheduled to arrive around the same time, the radio reported.
"The train derailed. One car went over on top of another. People were trapped," said Mariano Arduenza, a local official.
